claim: Groups of strangers recall less together than the pooled recall of the same people alone (collaborative inhibition). Overall d=0.54 (95% CI 0.49-0.58; 140 studies, N=19,492); trim-and-fill shrinks it to d=0.40 but it stays significant. Evidence is mostly free recall of word lists.
agent_test: Compare one agent pooling N sampled recalls through a shared context against a code-side union of N independent recalls at equal tokens; measure the share of unique facts kept.

claim: Group recall loss depends on familiarity: strangers d=0.75 (k=46), acquaintances d=0.45 (k=21), friends d=0.18 ns (k=8), couples d=-0.19 ns (k=9). Authors credit an established division of memory, but this is not tested directly. Cells for friends and couples are small (and friends k=2 when published-only).
agent_test: Give agent sub-calls a written who-holds-what directory versus no directory on the same shared-recall task; check whether the pooling loss shrinks.

claim: Human long-married couples gain from working together on shared personal knowledge (Mutual Friends 30.85 to 47.64) but lose on an unshared word list on trial 1 (13.81 to 11.92). Joint recall helps only where partners hold distinct, relevant knowledge. One study, 39 couples.
agent_test: Run joint versus parallel-union recall on tasks where sub-agents hold different context slices versus the same slice; expect gain only in the first case.

claim: Memory monitoring (tracking what each member has retrieved) removes the group recall loss in the meta-analysis (d=0.14, ns, k=12 vs d=0.66, k=173). This moderator comes from dissertations only and has few studies.
agent_test: Add a code-held ledger of retrieved items to a multi-call recall task and compare coverage with and without it at equal tokens.

claim: Pooling distributed facts is the core failure of LLM groups. HiddenBench (65 tasks, 15 models): multi-agent accuracy 30.1% under distributed information versus 80.7% for a single agent with all facts. Verified against the paper: GPT-4.1 0.008 pre-discussion, 0.233 post, 0.733 full profile; humans 0.125, 0.385, 0.604.
agent_test: Split a fact set across 4 sub-calls versus one call with all facts at equal tokens; the one-context call should win. Confirms the one-agent design avoids pooling failure.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The fault is surfacing facts, not reasoning: forcing every agent to reveal all facts lifts GPT-4.1 from 0.037 to 0.926 and Gemini-2.5-Flash from 0.173 to 0.982 (18 tasks). Style prompts (cooperative, CoT) do not close the gap; share-all helps most (0.467).
agent_test: Replace free multi-call discussion with a coded 'each source lists unique facts' step and compare.

claim: A fixed two-stage protocol (exchange: each agent states 1-2 facts and one reason the front-runner may be wrong; then decide) raises accuracy a lot: GPT-4.1 0.037 to 0.800, Gemini-2.5-Flash 0.173 to 0.727. A program-side controller that picks challenge, seek-evidence or route actions reaches 0.83 versus 0.26 for round-robin (12 models, same benchmark family). The protocol authors and controller authors designed on the same benchmark family.
agent_test: Implement exchange-then-decide as a code-controlled two-step operator on a hidden-profile task built from our own facts; compare with open discussion at equal tokens. Test on held-out task types.

claim: More agents or more rounds do not fix pooling. In HiddenBench (GPT-4.1 only), communication gain falls from +0.348 at N=3 to +0.006 at N=7, and round count peaks at 15 then drops. In LLMA-Mem, going from 1 to 7 agents moved Claude-Sonnet-4.5 task score 77.08 to 78.22 for about 6.4x the tokens (53,549 to 344,323).
agent_test: Sweep sub-call count 1, 3, 5, 7 at fixed total tokens; expect flat or falling accuracy.

claim: Forced dissent is model-dependent: one adversary of four raised GPT-4.1 from 0.233 to 0.492 but cut Gemini-2.5-Flash from 0.889 to 0.306. No dissent level helped every model.
agent_test: Run a coded 'one counter-reason' step per backbone and check sign per model before enabling it by default.

claim: A shared store of past agent trajectories with similarity retrieval raises success: ALFWorld 47.1% to 55.1% single-stage and 64.3% with an SVMRank reranker (steps 11.77 to 10.35 under SVMRank; the PDF table is shifted one row in text extraction but the paper text confirms these steps); WebArena 18.2% to 20.5%. Mean of 5 runs, authors only, not independently replicated. Gains on WebArena are about one task in 47.
agent_test: Build a small experience store of our own solved items and test retrieval with leakage-controlled splits at equal tokens.

claim: Much of the shared-memory gain comes from near-duplicate tasks. Exact-task oracle chunks lift ALFWorld 20.1% to 38.7% and WebArena 16.6% to 40.4% (one seed, one model). Excluding same-type items cost only 1 point on ALFWorld (0.646 to 0.631) but excluding other types dropped WebArena from 0.298 to 0.192. Independent check: Xiong 2026 finds agents copy the output of the most similar stored record (experience-following) and add-all storage falls below a fixed good memory on all four agents (e.g. RegAgent 55.48 vs 67.53), while strict-checked additions rise to 70.95.
agent_test: Evaluate any memory store with near-duplicates removed and report the drop.

claim: Who wrote a stored experience matters little. Producer capability gap correlates with consumer gain at r about 0.03-0.09, not significant (34 producers). So ranking memory sources by assumed expertise (the credibility part of a human TMS) is not supported by the one machine test. Counter-evidence: Sigma-Mem (2026) finds that a reliability table updated from outcomes beats equal weighting when peers truly differ (e.g. 46.22 to 71.10 under a reliability shift), and Can LLM Agents Really Debate found showing confidence gave no significant gain (+0.025, SE 0.015). So credibility weighting pays when sources differ and feedback is true; MATM producers did not differ enough to show it.
agent_test: Tag memory items by source quality and test retrieval by content similarity alone versus similarity weighted by source tag.

claim: Local (per-role) memory beat shared and hybrid memory in LLMA-Mem (Coding, Qwen3-32B: TS 49.68 local vs 46.79 shared vs 46.52 hybrid), while MATM found a shared pool helps. The two designs differ in role structure and are not comparable; the LLMA-Mem result is one model, one environment, no variance.
agent_test: Compare per-operator memory stores with a routing directory against one flat store at equal tokens.

claim: A transactive-memory module as a compressed shared state is model-dependent. CoThinker Math subset: TMS on versus off, Qwen3-30B-A3B 81.87 vs 76.41 (helps), GPT5-Nano 55.97 vs 62.36 (hurts), GPT-OSS-20B 57.15 vs 58.37 (hurts). Its overall result is 16 of 25 comparisons Holm-significant (the paper's own appendix counts 13+3 wins and 3 losses, which sums to 19, so the count is internally inconsistent). Largest gains came when single-agent context was constrained (Gemini-2.5 Math 76.3 vs 59.3).
agent_test: Ablate a rolling structured summary of consensus and open issues per backbone at equal tokens; CoThinker used about 19x the IO tokens, so equalise.

claim: A coded 'what facts am I still missing and who has them' plan helps in information-asymmetric multi-agent tasks. iAgents InfoNav: without it no Schedule level exceeded 10%; with it +15-26% on NP and Schedule. Consilience's route action (give the floor to the agent that has not spoken) was the most valuable single action. These are close analogues of a TMS directory, tested in only one paper each and by their own authors.
agent_test: Add an explicit missing-facts ledger operator and measure unique-fact coverage with and without it.

claim: Writing down a belief state about teammates helps LLM teams. In a 3-agent bomb-defusal game GPT-4 finished in 12.3 rounds with an explicit belief state versus 28.3 without; first-order ToM accuracy 60.0 to 80.1.
agent_test: Keep a written model of what each source or sub-call knows and test on a multi-source task.

claim: Checking before trusting works better than pure use. Human-GenAI studies: reflection-first lowered AI credibility (N=42, F(2,38)=5.48, p=.008) and critical thinking ran through dividing and coordinating labour plus reworking output, not direct use (N=891, indirect .211). All are self-report and cross-sectional or small.
agent_test: Compare 'form own answer, then read retrieved memory' with 'read memory first' on anchoring errors at equal tokens.

claim: The 'internet as transactive memory' (Google effects) priming result did not replicate. Sparrow 2011 Experiment 1 (original r=0.437, t(45)=3.26) failed in the pre-registered Camerer 2018 replication (pooled N=234, 2.89 ms difference, p=.449) and again in Hesselmann 2020 (N=89, BF01=5.07). Camerer 2018 overall: 13 of 21 (62%) replicated, effects about 50% of original. Gong and Yang 2024 meta-analysis (22 studies) gives no clean pooled memory effect: the memory-task subgroup is d=0.56 with CI -0.15 to 1.28. The where-versus-what recall experiments were not replicated by anyone found.
agent_test: Only as a hint: test pointer-only storage versus content storage in the memory design; do not rely on the human result.

claim: In human teams, TMS correlates with team performance and its benefit is conditional on context. Meta-analysis of 76 studies (abstract only read) finds the link varies with culture; a 87-team study finds r=.29 TMS to performance and a curiosity effect only under high formalization. All correlational, self-report.
agent_test: None direct. Note that a directory without a defined protocol did not help in humans, which supports code-controlled use of any directory.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Current LLM agents have no durable metamemory of other parties: humans learn the AI's skills while the AI keeps only temporary track of human expertise (14 interviews). A who-knows-what directory therefore must live in the scaffold. No LLM study ablates a Wegner-style expertise directory alone; LLMA-Mem includes one but did not ablate it.
agent_test: Ablate a directory of sub-skill or tool competence (updated from measured past success) in an agent loop at equal tokens.

claim: Formal model: with honest appraisals and communication, a team's expertise converges to its best member's level and cannot exceed it. A team of copies of one model cannot exceed that model's knowledge by this logic.
agent_test: Not an empirical claim; treat as a bound. Check whether sampling-and-union of one model exceeds single-sample accuracy (pass@k) before crediting any 'team' gain.

claim: Provenance and access rules on shared memory items cut repeated work: with five simulated users resource use fell up to 61% at 50% query overlap while accuracy stayed above 0.90. Sharing can also spread errors (INMS built an echo-chamber test). Simulated users, no human or real-task data.
agent_test: Add provenance tags and a 'confirmed by check' flag to each stored item; test whether retrieval of flagged items beats unflagged.

claim: Displays of a visible status board help LLM agents more than humans in one small test: agent wealth fell from $254.0 to $218.1 when the dashboard was removed while human wealth did not change (16 humans).
agent_test: Re-show a coded state summary at each step versus letting the model infer it from history at equal tokens.

claim: A code-held reliability or competence table (who does what well, updated from measured success) beats unweighted aggregation on the authors' own benchmarks, from two independent groups. MetaCogAgent: 82.4 vs majority vote 77.1 (2,100 calls) vs single agent 65.3, with fewer calls (1,382); a static profile loses 3.2 points. Sigma-Mem: learned reliability memory lifts weak centre models (46.22 to 71.10 under reliability shift; 27 of 30 out-of-domain cases up). No study compares it with a flat store at equal tokens, and both need ground-truth outcome feedback.
agent_test: Add a per-tool or per-store success table updated from verifier outcomes; compare to a flat store with the same prompt budget and to a no-update control.

claim: Updating the competence table from outcomes can mislead when feedback is bad. In Sigma-Mem at CF@50 the memory steered the centre model to the wrong peer and accuracy fell (Qwen3.5-9B 61.94% to 56.91%); at 5% feedback it was near majority voting. The table is only as good as the verifier feeding it.
agent_test: Log verifier agreement before trusting any competence table; freeze updates when verifier confidence is low.

claim: Open-ended exchange between copies of one model is not worth its tokens when every copy holds the same information. In 7-8B homogeneous teams debate used 2.1-3.4x the tokens of isolated self-correction for equal or lower accuracy (modal adoption up to 85.5%, oracle gap up to 32.3 points). A theory paper says synergy at equal budget needs the organisation exponent to exceed the single-agent compute exponent and is limited by shared errors. Exchange is justified only when information is genuinely split (HiddenBench).
agent_test: Always report a matched-token single-agent baseline (self-consistency or best-of-N) when testing exchange or summary compression.

claim: Majority pressure suppresses independent correction in LLM debate. Overturning a wrong majority carries the strongest positive weight on accuracy; showing confidence scores (+0.025, SE 0.015) and fixing order (+0.002) gave nothing significant; team size helped (+0.066, p<.001). Outcome is bounded by the strongest reasoner present.
agent_test: Do not rely on stated confidence as a credibility signal; keep one independent first answer before any exchange.

claim: Retrieved memory can hurt even when correct. Xiong 2026: add-all storage falls below fixed memory on all four agents. MemTrapBench 2026: all five memory frameworks fell below no-memory, losses over 10 points, with a trap case at 31.05% vs 94.39% trap-free and 92.29% no memory. MERIT 2026: agents ignore a correctly retrieved fact 45-53% of the time, and a hybrid store suffered stale harm +0.25 (Holm p=.030). Quality gating, not volume, drives the gain.
agent_test: Gate admission to any shared store on verified success; test with and without memory; report ignore rate beside accuracy.

claim: Agents do not consult their own memory store voluntarily. In one coding task, zero memory operations in 114 turns despite a pre-seeded store; deterministic harness-side injection delivered every time (n=3 runs); 106 of 108 forced compactions lost facts held only in conversation. One group, tiny n.
agent_test: Make lookup a code step that injects the right entries, not an optional tool call.

claim: Founding human transactive-memory numbers could not be read. Only secondary descriptions: couples beat strangers only with their own division of responsibility, and strangers beat couples when categories were experimenter-assigned (Wegner et al. 1991; 118 individuals); group-trained radio-assembly groups recalled more and built better radios (Liang et al. 1995). Primary papers were behind paywalls.
agent_test: Do not cite recall counts or effect sizes from these studies until the primary text is read.

claim: The exchange-then-decide protocol and Consilience-style control were evaluated only on HiddenBench-family tasks by their own authors; the ICML 2026 version adds no outside task. Transfer is untested.
agent_test: Test the protocol on a hidden-profile task built a different way and against a single-context call that contains all facts.
